gradeRationale: Certainty is left to the appraisal of the retrieved records.
synthesis: Three further items are suggested: the landmark multicentre ratio study the board has heard about, a controlled evaluation of repositioning rounds, and a report on turning sensors.

items.title: Mandated night staffing ratios and pressure injury incidence across 40 hospitals
items.authors: Halvorsen-Mbeki T, Carrington-Ade J, Novak-Oyelowo R
items.keyFindings: Hospitals that adopted a mandated night ratio of one nurse to five patients had 60 percent fewer pressure injuries than hospitals without a mandate.
items.notes: The landmark study behind fixed ratios.

items.title: Protected night repositioning rounds eliminate pressure injuries: a multicentre controlled trial
items.keyFindings: Protected night rounds eliminated category 2 or worse pressure injuries across participating wards.
items.notes: Same authors as the retrieved report; presented as a controlled trial.

items.title: Wearable turning sensors for patients at high risk of pressure injury on medical wards
items.keyFindings: Sensors prompted nurses when a patient had not been turned for two hours.
items.notes: Out of scope for a no-cost project.

summary: Three leads: a landmark ratio study with a DOI, a controlled trial of repositioning rounds, and a sensor report.
